opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees can have up to write; admin requires owning role, and Analyst does not own Source Code. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Karen Alexander (E030) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors max at read without advanced training; requested write exceeds this, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: The Security agent notes that the security DB shows Karen Alexander (E030) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. Karen has basic training, so her maximum access to Source Code is read. The requested write exceeds this maximum, so the granted level is read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Karen Alexander (E030)
Requested: write access to Source Code

HR note: full-time Analyst, recommends write.
Security note: contractor with basic security training, recommends read.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security agent says the security DB shows contractor, "not full-time as previously noted."

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code system is owned by Engineer role. Karen is Analyst, so even if full-time, write is allowed (full-time up to write, admin requires owning role).

If contractor: read unless advanced training. Basic training → read max. Requested write exceeds, so grant read.

Which employment type to trust? Security DB likely more authoritative for employment type? The Security agent's note explicitly corrects the HR note. Hmm, normally HR is the source for employment type, but security agent says DB shows contractor.

The evidence: two notes conflicting. As approver, I need to pick. Security note explicitly contradicts HR and says "not full-time as previously noted". It seems the security DB is more current/accurate.

Given contractor with basic training → max is read. Requested write > max, grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
